about: Component decisions a design engineer makes: which component fits the job, why, when the alternative wins, and what to avoid. 'n' is the number of options or items when the question has one. Read by design.py choose.

rules.need: pick one option from a set
rules.words: choose pick select one single option options either radio dropdown plan shipping method type size country language category role status

bands.use: switch (if it turns something on or off and applies at once) or a 2-option radio / segmented control
bands.why: both choices stay visible; one tap

bands.use: radio group (segmented control if labels are 1-2 words and it switches a view)
bands.why: every option is visible and comparable without opening anything
too many to show at once but short enough to scan in a list
nobody scrolls 15+ items; typing narrows it fast

rules.instead: Options that need description or comparison (plans, shipping speeds): radio cards. Choice affects only a view: segmented control or tabs.
rules.avoid: a dropdown for 2-4 options; a radio list of 30 countries; a select with no default when one is clearly most common

rules.words: multiple many several multi select tags interests filters permissions checkboxes features toppings categories

bands.why: everything visible; checkboxes say 'any number' clearly
searchable, and the chosen ones stay visible

rules.instead: Filters on a results page: checkbox groups in a filter panel with counts. Assigning items to two lists: a transfer list.
rules.avoid: a multi-select native <select> (hard on every device); switches for options that only apply after a Save button

rules.need: turn a setting on or off
rules.words: toggle switch enable disable on off setting preference notification notifications dark mode
rules.use: switch when the change applies immediately; checkbox when it applies after Save or is part of a form
rules.why: a switch promises instant effect; a checkbox promises 'part of what you submit'
rules.instead: Two named states that are not on/off (monthly / yearly): segmented control.
rules.avoid: a switch inside a form that needs Save; a checkbox that silently applies at once

rules.need: delete or do something hard to undo
rules.words: delete remove destroy cancel subscription close account archive discard reset irreversible destructive confirm
rules.use: reversible: do it and offer Undo in a toast; irreversible: a confirmation dialog that names what is lost, with a red button that says the action ('Delete project')
rules.why: confirmations people click through by habit protect nothing; undo protects without slowing everyone down
rules.instead: Very high stakes (deleting an organization): require typing the name.
rules.avoid: 'Are you sure?' with OK/Cancel; confirming reversible actions; the destructive button focused by default

rules.need: tell the user the result of something
rules.words: message feedback success error saved saving save after submit submitted sent done confirmation notify notification alert toast banner warning status result outcome
rules.use: inline message next to the thing (form errors, field validation); toast for the result of a user action that is done (Saved, with Undo); banner for a state of the whole page or account (offline, trial ending)
rules.why: feedback belongs where the eyes already are; toasts disappear, so never put something the user must act on in one
rules.instead: Blocking problem that stops the task: inline error plus focus on it, not a modal.
rules.avoid: toasts for errors that need action; modals for success; color as the only signal

rules.words: records items list table grid cards rows products orders users invoices results collection catalog gallery feed
rules.use: table when people compare values across items or sort by columns; list when they scan one main attribute and open items; cards when items are visual (photos, products) or have very different content
rules.why: the layout should match the task: comparing needs columns, browsing needs images, scanning needs a list
rules.instead: On phones, a table of more than 3 columns becomes stacked cards or a list with the key values.
rules.avoid: cards for data people need to compare; tables for photo-heavy items; identical cards with no scannable anchor

rules.need: show a long set of items
rules.words: pagination paginate infinite scroll load more long list hundreds thousands many results page
rules.use: pagination for work data people return to or reference (tables, search results); 'load more' button for browsing; infinite scroll only for endless feeds with no footer
rules.why: pagination keeps position and URLs; infinite scroll loses both and hides the footer
rules.instead: Very long lists that must stay on one page: virtualize the list.
rules.avoid: infinite scroll on tables or search results; pagination with no total count

rules.words: tabs sections views navigate switch between pages sidebar menu steps wizard sequence navigation

bands.use: tabs (peer views of the same thing)
bands.why: all views visible; one click to switch; no page change

bands.use: sidebar or top navigation (or a select on phones)
bands.why: more than 5 tabs wrap or scroll and hide options

rules.instead: Steps that must happen in order: a stepper or wizard with back and progress. Sections the user reads in order: one page with headings and an on-page outline.
rules.avoid: tabs for sequential steps; tabs whose content depends on another tab; hamburger menus on desktop

rules.need: show more detail or a secondary task
rules.words: details more info expand collapse preview edit popup modal dialog drawer side panel accordion disclosure overlay inspector quick view
rules.use: disclosure or accordion for optional detail on the same page; drawer (side panel) for a task that needs the page as context (edit a row, preview); modal dialog only for a short task that must interrupt; its own page for anything long, linkable, or multi-step
rules.why: modals block context and are hard on phones; pages can be linked, refreshed, and navigated back from
rules.instead: Peek on hover is only an extra; the same detail must be reachable by click or keyboard.
rules.avoid: long forms in modals; modals that open modals; essential content hidden in a collapsed accordion

rules.words: date birthday dob time schedule booking appointment calendar range deadline due reservation check-in
rules.use: known dates far away (birthday, expiry): text fields or a typed date with a clear format; near-future scheduling: calendar picker showing availability; ranges (stays, reports): range picker with presets
rules.why: scrolling a calendar to 1987 is slow; picking next Tuesday from a calendar is fast
rules.instead: Times: a list of available slots beats a free time input for bookings.
rules.avoid: calendar-only entry with no typing; ambiguous formats like 03/04; a picker that hides the time zone

rules.words: number quantity amount count price budget range slider stepper percentage volume rating
rules.use: stepper (minus / input / plus) for small counts (quantity 1-10); slider with a visible value for approximate choices on a range (volume, budget estimate); text input with inputmode=decimal for exact values (prices, amounts)
rules.why: sliders are imprecise and hard for keyboards and tremors; steppers suit small changes
rules.instead: Ratings: 5 labelled radio buttons styled as stars.
rules.avoid: a slider for exact amounts; type=number for codes, card numbers, or phone numbers

rules.need: show that something is loading or running
rules.words: loading spinner progress skeleton waiting upload processing fetching pending busy
rules.use: under 1s: nothing; 1-3s: a spinner or pressed state where the action happened; content loads: skeletons shaped like the result; known duration or over 10s: a progress bar with what is happening, and let the user leave and get notified
rules.why: feedback should match the wait; skeletons prevent layout jumps
rules.instead: Optimistic updates for actions that almost always succeed (like, rename).
rules.avoid: full-page spinners for one widget; buttons that change width when loading; spinners with no end

rules.words: help hint tooltip explain info description guidance instructions label onboarding tip
rules.use: visible hint text under the field or heading for anything the user needs; tooltip only to name an icon-only control or add non-essential detail
rules.why: tooltips are invisible on touch and easy to miss; needed information must be on the page
rules.instead: Complex concepts: a 'Learn more' link to a help page, or an inline expandable explanation.
rules.avoid: essential instructions in tooltips or placeholders; info icons on every field

rules.need: place the main actions of a page or form
rules.words: button buttons action actions cta call to action submit save primary secondary
rules.use: one primary button per view, named with verb and object ('Save changes'); secondary actions as quieter buttons; destructive actions separated
rules.why: two primary buttons means no primary action
rules.instead: Many actions on one item: a menu ('...') with the most common one left out as a button.
rules.avoid: several primary buttons; disabled submit buttons with no explanation; 'OK' / 'Submit' labels

rules.words: search find filter filters sort browse lookup query facets narrow
rules.use: search box when users know what they want (a name, an ID); filters when they explore by attributes (price, size, status); both on large catalogs, with search first
rules.why: search serves known items, filters serve exploration
rules.instead: Under ~20 items: no search, just a sorted list.
rules.avoid: filters that reset when you search; search without showing the query and result count

rules.need: show several featured items, images, or messages
rules.words: carousel slider slideshow hero rotating banner gallery featured testimonials images
rules.use: a static grid or a horizontally scrollable row with visible overflow (the next item peeks); one hero, not a rotating set
rules.why: auto-rotating carousels hide content, get few clicks after slide one, and are hard to control
rules.instead: A photo gallery: a grid that opens a lightbox with keyboard and swipe support.
rules.avoid: auto-advancing slides; dots as the only control; key information on slide 3
